title: SRE weekly ops sync prep — 2026-03-26 (draft)
body:
Purpose: prep notes for SRE weekly ops sync + reliability review (SLO status, paging trends, top incidents, action items).

Meeting logistics:
- Time: Thu 2026-03-26 10:00-11:00 PT
- Attendees: SRE on-call rotation, infra eng, serving-runtime, product-ops, on-call manager
- Goal: surface regressions, align on mitigations and rollout windows, confirm owners for follow-ups

Agenda (50m total):
1) Quick status (10m) — on-call: current alerts, notable pages since last sync
2) SLO review (10m) — availability + latency trends, burn rates
3) Paging trends (10m) — channel breakouts, noisy alert rules to tune
4) Top incidents postmortems (15m) — highlight RCA and next steps for last 3 incidents
5) Action items & blockers (5m) — assign owners, due dates

Quick status notes (to call out):
- On-call reports ~+35% pages week-over-week (mainly late-night pages from eu-west-1).
- Current on-call fatigue risk flagged by Samira — consider short mitigation for schedule coverage if pages remain high next week.
- No active Sev1s at time of writing.

SLOs / Metrics (current snapshot):
- API availability (global successful response rate): SLO 99.95% monthly. Current 30-day rolling = 99.92% (slight SLO miss window on 2026-03-22).
- Latency SLOs: p95 < 120ms (SLO), p99 < 500ms (SLO). Current p95 = 135ms (up), p99 = 420ms.
- Error budget: remaining for the month ~0.03% (~consumed by March 22 incident).

Notes / interpretation:
- Latency increase correlated with increased KV cache miss rate and a spike in prefix eviction (see dashboard linked). The p99 remained within SLO but p95 drift is concerning for frontend user latency.
- Availability dip on 2026-03-22 caused primarily by model-serving OOMs when a canary of quantized v2 model hit a traffic spike. Autoscaler did not provision fast enough because the canary used exclusive GPU pool with lower burst policy.

Paging trends (root causes):
- Top noisy alerts: ReplicaDown, HighKVCacheMissRate, ModelOOM (recent), PersistedQueueDepthHigh.
- Channel distribution: ~60% pages to #sre-pages, 25% to #infra-alerts, 15% to #serving-runtime on-call.
- Time distribution: spike during eu-night (00:00-04:00 PT) — investigate if any cron or rollout window triggers here.

Top incidents since last sync (summary):
1) 2026-03-22 — Model-serving OOM (INC-2026-03-22-model-oom)\   - Impact: short outage for host-model endpoints in us-west-2 + increased 5xx for 18m\   - Root cause: canary of quantized v2 had different memory profile (missing kernel fallback), memory usage growth under specific prompt shapes -> OOM. Autoscaler pool policy prevented bursting into shared capacity.\   - Mitigation done: roll back canary, restart affected replicas, temporarily increase burst policy for dedicated pools.\   - Permanent actions: Add memory profile test in preflight (PR#905), update autoscaler policy to allow emergency burst for canaries, add synthetic load test for quantized variants. Owner: Aisha Khan. ETA: 2026-04-09.

2) 2026-03-24 — KV cache eviction storm -> p95 latency spike\   - Impact: p95 increased from 110ms to 220ms for ~2 hours across serving fleet\   - Root cause: unexpected increase in unique session prefixes after a product rollout; cache resize wasn't triggered; eviction churn caused more disk reads.\   - Mitigation done: temporarily raised in-memory cache cap for hot-tier; rebalanced hot partitions.\   - Permanent actions: implement adaptive cache resizing + alert for eviction-churn. Owner: Ethan Chen. ETA: 2026-04-02.

3) 2026-03-25 — Autoscaler warmup misconfig for dedicated pool (minor)\   - Impact: slower instance warmup causing brief throughput degradation during a 10m traffic spike\   - Root cause: warmup lifecycle change in cloud-init image (PR#897) not accounted for in autoscaler heuristics.\   - Mitigation done: manual scale, revert warmup heuristic change on staging while infra team patches heuristics.\   - Permanent actions: add warmup-time SLI and include warmup profile in CI. Owner: Samira Patel. ETA: 2026-03-30.

Open questions for wider team / product:
- Product: Was the rollout on 2026-03-24 expected to increase unique session prefixes? If so, we need advance warning of user segmentation changes so SRE can pre-adjust caches. (@product-ops)
- Infra: Can we get a short-term emergency policy for canaries that allows limited burst into shared pools? Need guardrails to avoid noisy neighbor issues.

Action items (tracked):
- Aisha: implement memory-profile preflight for quantized model variants + add synthetic tests (PR + test harness). Due 2026-04-09.
- Ethan: implement adaptive cache resizing + eviction-churn alert. Due 2026-04-02.
- Samira: add warmup-time SLI, update CI to fail on warmup regressions. Due 2026-03-30.
- Jordan (me): update alert runbook for HighKVCacheMissRate, include steps for temporary cap raise and rebalance playbook. Due 2026-03-29.
- On-call manager: review rota for next 2 weeks; consider adding an overnight backup for eu-west-1 windows. Due 2026-03-27.

Runbook / follow-up notes (quick wins):
- Tune alert thresholds for ReplicaDown -> reduce noisy false positives (current threshold too low for short GC pauses).
- Add synthetic p95 probe against a subset of hot endpoints to detect cache-related regressions earlier.
- Add a short post-deploy canary traffic spike test (10% burst) to validate autoscaler response for guarded canaries.

Notes to self (informal):
- Remember to bring up the idea of an "emergency-burst" tag for canaries during sync — need Prod buy-in.
- Keep monitoring eu-night pages next 48h; if still high, propose temporary schedule change for on-call.
- Follow up with infra on PR#897 heatmap of warmup times (need numbers to finalize SLI threshold).

Prep checklist for meeting:
- [x] link incident RCAs in doc (INC-2026-03-22, INC-2026-03-24).
- [x] snapshot SLO dashboard (last 30 days).
- [ ] confirm Samira can present autoscaler notes (ask @Samira today).
- [ ] prepare short note for product about cache impact of rollout (draft email).

End of notes. Will iterate after sync and convert this into a slim meeting minutes doc with explicit owners and dates (move to shared_drives/engineering/site-reliability-engineering after finalized).
